ra.short: The sky’s “longitude”, measured east in hours, minutes and seconds (24h = full circle).

dec.short: The sky’s “latitude”, from −90° at the south celestial pole to +90° at the north.

fov.short: How much sky the image covers, in arcminutes (′). Bigger fields catch faster movers but take longer to load.

arcsec.short: 1/3600 of a degree. The full Moon is about 1,800″ across; a SPHEREx pixel is 6.15″.

epoch.short: One visit to this patch of sky. SPHEREx revisits the whole sky about every six months.

band.short: A narrow slice of infrared wavelengths. SPHEREx records 102 of them, from 0.75 to 5.0 µm.

array.short: SPHEREx has six detectors, each covering a range of wavelengths. Stacking a whole array gives a cleaner image.

blink.short: Flipping between snapshots, the way Clyde Tombaugh found Pluto in 1930. Anything that jumps is moving.

difference.short: One snapshot subtracted from another. Fixed stars cancel out; movers leave a teal (was here) and amber (now here) pair.

stack.short: Averaging snapshots together. Noise drops, so faint still objects stand out, but movers smear.

pm.short: How fast a star drifts across the sky, in arcseconds per year. Nearby stars move most.

browndwarf.short: An object too heavy to be a planet but too light to burn like a star. Cold ones glow mainly in infrared.

variable.short: A star whose brightness changes over time, from pulsing, eclipses or passing dust.

flags.short: Markers on pixels affected by glitches such as cosmic rays, ghosts or glare. Flagged pixels are hidden.

zodi.short: Faint glow from dust in our Solar System. It changes with the seasons, so it is removed before comparing snapshots.

spectrum.short: Brightness at each wavelength. Dips reveal molecules such as water ice, methane or carbon dioxide.

gaia.short: ESA mission that measured positions and motions of almost 2 billion stars. Used to check whether a mover is already known.

wise.short: NASA infrared survey from 2010 onward. Catches cold objects Gaia can’t see.

release.short: A published batch of processed images. DR1 covers surveys 1–2; QR3 adds newer data every week.

candidate.short: A possible discovery waiting for a scientist to check it. Not confirmed until verified.
